subject.title: Telegram: allow native channel commands in explicitly allowed chats

question: For Telegram channel_post native and plugin commands, should senderless channel posts be allowed only by explicit channel chat authorization, or fail closed when sender-scoped allowFrom semantics cannot be evaluated?
rationale: The PR changes a command execution surface, while Telegram channel_post can lack a normal human sender and the paired open issue asks for a security policy decision that automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Fix Auth And Callback Semantics Before Merge
options.body: Require explicit channel authorization, sender_chat-aware allowlist behavior, channel-aware callback/session routing, and redacted live Telegram proof before landing this branch.

options.title: Pause For Policy Resolution
options.body: Use the paired channel_post auth policy issue to settle sender-scoped allowFrom semantics before this PR changes runtime behavior.

options.title: Accept Explicit-Chat-Only Semantics
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally accept explicit-chat-only channel_post commands, but should document the security rationale and prove the live Telegram path.

recommendation.title: Fix Auth And Callback Semantics Before Merge
recommendation.body: Require explicit channel authorization, sender_chat-aware allowlist behavior, channel-aware callback/session routing, and redacted live Telegram proof before landing this branch.

likelyOwner.reason: The related policy issue already routes the sender-scoped Telegram auth decision to this person based on adjacent auth/docs history.
